sections.name: review packet write boundary
sections.title: Packet write boundary tests
sections.what: Covers rejecting a cross-case result, rejecting bad input, keeping retrieval and edits scoped to one case, and locking a packet after it is ready.
sections.why: Protects packets from crossing case boundaries and from being edited after approval.
sections.watch_out: The lock test only runs its ready step when the packet starts as draft, so confirm that condition holds.

summary: Tests that review packets are created only from valid results in the same case, stay scoped to that case, and lock after being marked ready.
purpose: Protects packet integrity and case boundaries.
why: Likely reason: prevents packets from mixing cases and stops edits after approval.
how: Tests cover a cross-case result (expects 422), malformed input (expects 400), retrieval and edits from another case (expects 404), and an edit after marking ready (expects 409 PACKET_LOCKED).
inputs: Result ids and case ids from the seed data.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: The lock test contains an if statement. If the new packet is not in draft state, the ready step is skipped, so the lock test may not check what its name says.
debug: Read the packet service's status flow and confirm the new packet starts as draft.
